_what: The words of each email the sign-in sends, by the kind auth.mjs gives (otp-<type> for an email code, by Better Auth's emailOTP types; the link kinds by their callback). Each {field} is the message's own value: otp, url, newEmail, and minutes (settings.json email_code, the same minutes the pages say). send-email.mjs fills them; the provider gets them as subject and text.

otp-sign-in.subject: Your Trillion sign-in code: {otp}
text: Your code to sign in to Trillion is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask to sign in, you can ignore this email.

otp-email-verification.subject: Your Trillion code: {otp}
text: Your code to prove this address for Trillion is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

otp-forget-password.subject: Your Trillion password code: {otp}
text: Your code to set a new Trillion password is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, your password stays as it is.

otp-change-email.subject: Your Trillion code: {otp}
text: Your code to change your Trillion address is {otp}
It works for {minutes} minutes. If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

magic-link.subject: Sign in to Trillion
text: Open this link to sign in to Trillion:
{url}
If you did not ask to sign in, you can ignore this email.

reset-password.subject: Set a new Trillion password
text: Open this link to set a new Trillion password:
{url}
If you did not ask for it, your password stays as it is.

verify-email.subject: Prove your address for Trillion
text: Open this link to prove this address for Trillion:
{url}
If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.

change-email.subject: Change your Trillion address
text: Open this link to change your Trillion address to {newEmail}:
{url}
If you did not ask for it, your address stays as it is.
